title: Short Stuff: Mabon
summary: Short Stuff episode on Mabon, the neo-pagan harvest festival observed at the autumnal equinox, often called the pagan Thanksgiving. hosts cover the name's origin in a Welsh god and the Mabinogion, Aidan Kelly's modern addition to the wheel of the year linking it to Demeter, the balance theme of equal day and night, other harvest festivals (Lunasa, Samhain, Mabon), the Kukulkan pyramid shadow at Chichen Itza, and simple ways non-pagans can observe the day such as cornucopia centerpieces, reflection, and fall outings. Includes a digression on comedy (Tim Robinson) and a mention of Dave Roves's article and podcast.
topics: Chichen Itza Kukulkan pyramid equinox shadow

segments.title: Welcome and introduction to Mabon
segments.summary: Hosts introduce Mabon as the pagan Thanksgiving, a fall harvest celebration of the autumnal equinox, and note it is one of several harvest festivals and one of eight Sabbats on the wheel of the year.

segments.title: Harvest festivals and the equinox balance
segments.summary: Hosts describe the three harvest festivals from August through October (Lunasa, Mabon, Samhain) and explain that the equinox's equal day and night gives Mabon its theme of balance. They note Mabon is a modern addition and the name is about 55 years old, drawn from the Welsh figure Mabon, son of the Earth Mother, and the Mabinogion.

segments.title: Aidan Kelly, Demeter and the wheel of the year
segments.summary: Hosts explain that Aidan Kelly, who helped shape the modern pagan wheel of the year in the 1960s and 70s, chose the name Mabon because Demeter, celebrated at the equinox, shares a rescue-from-underworld story with Mabon. The ancient Celts did not mark the equinox, and the eight Sabbats include older Celtic festivals like Beltane and Imbolc.

segments.title: Equinox sun at Chichen Itza
segments.summary: Hosts discuss other cultures marking the equinox and describe the Pyramid of Kukulkan at Chichen Itza, where shadows create a serpent effect on the steps during the autumnal equinox.

segments.title: Eagle Rock anecdote
segments.summary: Chuck recounts that Eagle Rock, in the Los Angeles neighborhood of the same name, looks like a flying eagle when sunlight hits it at a certain time of day.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the practical advice section.

segments.title: Dave Roves article and tolerance
segments.summary: Josh says the episode is based on a HowStuffWorks article by Dave Roves and plugs Dave's podcast Biblical Time Machine.

segments.title: Celebrating Mabon: cornucopia and reflection
segments.summary: Hosts suggest ways to observe Mabon even without paganism: a cornucopia centerpiece with roots in ancient Greece, and reflecting on the past year, balance, gratitude, and releasing things, contrasted with Ostara's renewal theme.

segments.title: Tangent on Tim Robinson comedy
segments.summary: Conversation drifts to Tim Robinson and I Think You Should Leave sketches, including a clothing joke and the Ocean View Dining brand, with a playful suggestion of a Tim Robinson marathon as a Mabon activity.

segments.title: Fall activities for non-pagans
segments.summary: Hosts suggest fall color, dried flowers, walks, and corn mazes as ways to celebrate, and conclude that for non-pagans the goal is to feel good about fall.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the Short Stuff episode and note the iHeartRadio production credit.
